greet.text: Stop right there! Gold on you? Gold on you. Good. I'm {name} {clan}. Without that gold you'd be dead. Welcome!
Ooh! Shiny! You're shiny all over! Are you rich? Can I have a bit? Just a small bit?
Gold. Hrm. You live.
Gold, in our Bastion? Most outsiders come down here to take gold, not wear it. Speak, shiny one.
A stranger in {village}, and wearing gold! Wait. Stay here. I want to brag about you before the others see you.
Pink-skin. You glint, so you live. Talk fast. I'm busy being important.
Your gold's still on. Smart. Keep it on and we'll keep being polite.
The shiny one again! Ha! Gold still on, head still on. Good for both of us.
You came back! Most outsiders don't. Mostly because of us. Ha!
Ingot-friend! Come here! Your gold looks heavier than last time. Or I'm greedy. Both, probably.
Hoard-friend! I told {neighbour} you'd be back. They bet against you. Now they owe me three nuggets.
Tusk-kin! Everyone look! The finest gold-wearer in the Nether came to see ME!
My Tusk-kin! I'd know your shine from across a lava sea. Come, stand by me so they all see who my friends are.
Did you bring gold? Grown-ups say ask nicely. Gold, please! Now, please!
It's you! I told everyone you're my friend! {neighbour} said I was lying. Stand here so they can see.
*snort* Shiny! You're back! Can I hold your gold? I'll give it back. Probably.
You're not shiny today! That's fine. You're still my friend. The grown-ups might be grumpy, though.
Hrm.
Gold. Fine. Don't touch the Hoard.
You. Good. Stand near. Nobody bothers you here.
Vault's below. Not for you. Gold or no gold.
No gold. Hrm. Know your face. Others don't. Stay near.
Mind the floor. The fire ate half of it and we sold the rest. Ha! What do you want?
Gold-friend in the old halls! Come in, come in. There's a warm room the fire forgot to take.
Welcome to {village}! Loudest Hold in the Nether. Ask anyone. They'll shout it at you.
Got an ingot? I've got a deal. Got two? I've got a better deal. Got none? Got lost.
Stand in the light. Let me see your gold. Hm. Who made that? Sloppy rivets. I'd have done it better.
You smell like you've been near my pens. Good. The hoglins hate you a little less now.
Stand back from the furnace! Or don't. Your eyebrows, not mine. Mine are long gone.
Quiet! Oh. Just you. You walk heavy, like a hoglin. I nearly shot you. That's a compliment.
See this shroomlight? Pinched it off the warped canopy. Netted twice. Worth it. What do you want?
Another gold-wearer on the road! Then there are two of us out here. Ha! The other one's me.
Is that an ingot in your hand? For me? Say it's for me.
You're carrying a Hollowed skull. I can smell it. Throw it in the lava. Then we talk.
Gold! Good. What do you want? Speak up. I can't hear quiet folk.
Your gold catches the light nicely. Mine catches it better. What is it?
No gold on you? Bold. Lucky it's me you walked into. I know your face. The others only know gold.
Where's your gold? Hm. Friends don't need it, not with me. Stay close, though. {neighbour} doesn't know you like I do.
Ha! Bare as a Rotted bone, and I'm still glad to see you. That's how you know it's real.

greet: Oi! Shiny! Over here! What do you need?

chatter.text: Walking about with no gold. In the Nether. You trust me that much? Good. Don't trust the others that much.
{neighbour} said they could bite through a nugget. I said prove it. They broke a tusk. I won nine nuggets.
Last time {neighbour} tried to barter with a hoglin, the hoglin won. Took a boot and half a trouser leg.
If {neighbour} says they beat me at arm-wrestling, it's a lie. I let them. Twice. Three times.
I heard {neighbour} polished their helmet so hard it went thin. Now it dents if you look at it. So I look at it a lot.
I'm sure {neighbour} owes me an ingot from the last brawl. Or I owe them. I forget. I'll say they owe me.
Never eat {neighbour}'s porkchops. The last one who did is still running. Round and round and round.
So {neighbour} counted the Hoard twice and got two different numbers. Now we're all counting. Loudly.
You should hear {neighbour} sing at the hearth. The hoglins put up with it. That tells you how tough hoglins are.
{neighbour} says Overworld folk are soft. Are you soft?

replies.text: Ha! No, no. I'd win, and then we couldn't be friends. I'll tell them you're hard as blackstone.
Ha! Soft and honest. That's a rare pair. Still soft, though.
Me? Feel this arm! No, don't feel it. Just look at it. Hard as blackstone.

chatter.text: Gold doesn't rust, doesn't rot and doesn't lie. That's three things better than most Piglins I know.
I bit a gold nugget once to see if it was real. It was. Best tooth I ever lost.
A hoglin charged me once. I charged back. We both stopped. Stared. Now we nod at each other.
Brutes don't laugh. I made one laugh once. Then I ran, very fast. Still not sure why.
Ghasts shriek at the walls. I shout back. I think I'm winning.
Ever smelled a strider up close? No? Lucky. The Magmari ride them. That explains the Magmari.
Never throw gold in the lava. Never. I'd have to kill you, and then I'd be sad, and you'd be dead.
Iron? Pah. Iron is what you wear when you're poor and want everyone to know it.
I brought you nothing. I bring nothing to anybody. That's how I got rich.
The Rotted came near the edge again. We waved. They didn't wave back. They never wave back.
If the horn blows, run toward it if you're with us. Run away if you're not. Easy rule.
You stand like a fighter. Are you a fighter?

replies.text: Ha! A boaster! Boasters fight hardest. They've got so much to live up to.
HA! Not now. Later. After I've eaten. I fight better full.
Then stand like a sack, so nobody gets fooled.

chatter.text: Do you like my helmet? Be honest. No, be nice.

replies.text: MAGNIFICENT! Hear that? Everyone hear that?
Lies! Beautiful lies. Let me see. Hm. Fine. Close.
Dents are stories! You've got no dents. So no stories. Hmph.

chatter.text: Tell me true. How much gold have you got?

replies.text: Ha! A lie, but a bold one. I respect a bold liar.
Then barter with me. I'll make you rich. Richer. A bit.
Gold is EVERYONE'S business! Rude.

chatter.text: I'm the strongest in this Hold. Agreed?

replies.text: Smart! Say it louder when {neighbour} walks past.
Ha! I lifted a hoglin once. A small one. It still counts.
Brutes are BIGGER. Not stronger. Big difference. Go away.

chatter.text: Overworld folk wear iron, I heard. All grey. Is it true?

replies.text: Grey! Like ash! Poor things. Bring them here. We'll shine them up.
Useful! Rocks are useful! Nobody wears rocks!

chatter.text: My father had the biggest tusks in the {clan}. Mine are bigger. I measured. He disagrees. Loudly.
My mother could out-shout a ghast. I can out-shout my mother. That's how the {clan} gets louder every litter.
You're carrying a gold block. I can smell it. Don't ask how. Just know that I know.
Why do you smell like the Rotted? Scrub yourself. Scrub twice. With ash.
This was the grandest place in the Nether. Then the fire. Now it's the grandest ruin. Still grand.
The stones are still warm in the deep rooms. We sleep on those. Best beds in the Nether. Only beds, too.
{neighbour} found a lump of melted gold in the rubble. Shaped like a hoglin, if you squint. We all squint.
Barter tip: shout. Whoever shouts last wins. I always shout last. I've got the lungs for it.
Fresh hoglin tracks by the fungus. Big one. Mine. Don't even look at it.
Crimson fungus, warped fungus, nether wart. I can tell them apart by smell. Can you? Don't sniff that one.
Melt it, beat it, wear it, boast about it. That's goldsmithing. The boasting is the hard part.
My eyebrows have burned off three times. They grow back angrier every time.
My hoglins have names. Bitey, Bitey Two and Snorrk. Snorrk bites most. Don't tell the Biteys.
Every Hold says it's the loudest Hold. I've heard them all. They're all right. It's very loud out here.
Hrm.
Gate stays shut.
Thieves. I smell them. Not you. Yet.
Gold on you. Good. Keep it on.
Axe is sharp. Sharpened it. Twice.
You. Fight?

replies.text: Hrm! Good. Later.
Hrm. Smart.

chatter.text: I found a nugget! It's mine! You can look. Don't touch. Fine, touch. Gently.
Watch me run with gold! *snort snort* Nobody can catch me! Except grown-ups. And Brutes.
I rode a baby hoglin! It bit my ear. Worth it. Want to see the ear?
{neighbour} says I'm too small to wear gold. I'm going to wear SO much gold. All of it.
Are you rich? You look rich.

replies.text: Wow! Can I be rich too? Will you show me how?
Then why are you shiny? Is it pretend gold? Can I bite it?

lines.text: I am {name} {clan}! Say it back. Louder. Good. Now you'll remember it.
{name} of the {clan}. Best clan in the Nether. Every clan says that. We say it loudest, so we win.
The {clan} name is older than the fire. We lost the bastions, the gold, half our tusks. We kept the name. Names don't melt.
I'm {name}, {job}, of the {clan}. And you're the pink-skin who wears gold. What are you to us?

replies.text: Ha! Bold. I like bold. Keep saying it until it's true.
Nobody just passes through wearing gold. Gold always means something.
Nobody special doesn't wear gold. Stand up straight. You're shaming your helmet.

lines.text: Between us? My grandsire won the {clan} name in a bet. Still counts. A bet is a bet. Don't tell the clan.
{name}. {clan}. Brute. Enough.

lines: Gold is rank. More gold, more say. Less gold, less say. No gold, no say. Also no head.
Gold is savings. It doesn't rot, it doesn't rust, it doesn't run off. It just sits there being beautiful.
Gold is the handshake. You show gold, I show gold, nobody stabs anybody. That's peace, the Piglin way.
We first wore it in the war, so we'd know our own in the smoke. Nobody else would touch the stuff. Still true. Except you.

lines.text: First you tell me. What is gold to you?

replies.text: EVERYTHING! Yes! You understand! I knew it the moment you shone!
Trading, yes. That's the second-best thing gold does. The first is shining.
Just shiny... Out of my sight. No. Stay. I'll fix you. It'll take a while.

lines.text: {village}! Three longhouses, one Hoard, one horn, and the loudest barter ring this side of the lava.
The barter ring is the heart of the Hold. Gold block on the pedestal. Touch it and find out what we're like. Actually, don't.
Longhouse life: one hearth, one gold block, too many Piglins, all snoring. You get used to it. Or you go deaf. Same thing.
Climb the horn tower if you like. The Brute up top won't stop you. He'll just stare until you climb back down.
The forge is where the gold gets pretty. Don't touch the cauldron. It's lava, not soup. {neighbour} learned that one.
This was a bastion, the greatest in the Nether. Then the Wither came. Outsiders call it a Remnant now. We call it home.
See the black on the walls? Soot from the fire. We never scrubbed it off. Some things you keep where you can see them.
Our Bastion. Burned, broken, ours. What do you think of it?

replies.text: Even burned! Even burned it's better than anything up in your rotting world.
Everything needs work. You need work. Ha!
A RUIN? It's a home with a bad past. Watch your mouth this close to the lava.

lines.text: This? This is nowhere. Lava and fungus. My Hold is wherever my gold is, and my gold is on me.
Out here there's no horn to call your friends. Just me, my crossbow and my mouth. The mouth works best.
I run the barter ring. You give gold, I give things. Which things? Whatever the gold decides. Gold has moods.
Bartermaster. I'm fair, I'm fast, and if you argue I count slower. Want a tip?

replies.text: Never show your whole purse. Show a bit, and look sad. Not with me, though. You're with me.
Ha! Everyone needs tips. That's why I'm rich and you're the one asking.

lines.text: I hunt wild hoglins in the crimson. Not the penned ones. Those are herd. Mean herd, but herd.
Crossbow, quiet feet, and a lot of shouting at the end. That's hunting. The shouting is the best part.
Fungus, wart, quartz, shroomlight. If it grows or glints out there, I bring it home and brag about it.
The best shroomlights hang in the warped canopy. The Weft drop nets on you. Worth it. Mostly. Once it wasn't.
I melt raw gold into ingots. Hot work. Good work. Smell my bristles. That's the smell of success.
The blast furnace roars, I roar back. The gold comes out shining. My eyebrows never come out at all.
I make the armour that keeps gold-wearers alive down here. Every Piglin in this Hold wears my work. You may bow a little.
Gold is soft. That's the trick. You don't fight it. You talk to it, hit it, then talk to it again.
I keep the pens. Crimson fungus in, warped fungus far away, fingers attached. That's the whole job.
Penned hoglins are herd, not game. Nobody hunts them. You want one for the fire, you ask me. Then I say no.
Guard. Gate. Gold. Three words. Good job.
Stand. Watch. Hit thieves. Don't sit.
Work? I live in a bastion the Wither burned. Staying alive in it is the work.
We sweep the ash, guard the old vault, and fight over who sleeps in the warm rooms. I always win.
I walk from Hold to Hold carrying news. News costs a nugget. That bit was free.
No Hold of my own. I sleep wherever my gold is safe. Usually on top of it.

lines: Piglins who went through to your world. They came back green, slow and gold-blind. That's what your world does to us.
Your world rots us. Everyone knows it. Somehow it doesn't rot you. Suspicious. Very suspicious.
Don't hit the Rotted. Hit one and they all come. They forgot their names. They didn't forget each other.

lines.text: You came out of the Overworld and you smell fine. How?

replies.text: Born in the rot and not rotted. Huh. Maybe it's slow. Check your ears now and then.
Tougher than a Piglin? Ha! No. But I like the nerve. Keep it.
Don't say that! Stand over there. Further. Further.

lines.text: My uncle went through a portal after gold. He came back Rotted. He still walks the wastes. I wave. He doesn't.

replies.text: Don't be sorry. Be careful. Keep your gold on and stay out of portals. Well. You came out of one.
HAPPY? He's rotting on his feet! Don't joke about the Rotted. Not to me. Not ever.

lines: There was gold under the soul valleys. Rivers of it. The Withren sat on it and called it theirs. Sitting on a thing doesn't make it yours.
The Magmari carried our war-bands over the lava seas. For pay. Then they wept when it went wrong. They should have charged more.
After every fight the Weft crept in and took bones. Ours and theirs. Their looms still click with our grandsires.
We wore gold so we'd know our own in the smoke. Nobody else would wear it. That's why gold-wearers live here and the rest don't.

lines.text: We were winning. Remember that. Whatever the ash-faces tell you, we were winning.

replies.text: Good. Gold-wearing AND smart. Rare.
Then the Withren cheated. Ask me about the fire some time. Not yet. When I trust you more.
WERE WE? We were winning with our TUSKS! Go away before I show you!

lines: The Withren made a monster out of three of their own. The Last Answer, they call it. Answer to what? To us. We were the question.
It came over the wastes with three heads screaming. The bastions went up like kindling. Gold ran down the walls like lava.
It didn't stop with us. It burned the Moorings, then the Withren's own forts. They made a thing that ate its makers. Ha. Not funny. A bit funny.

lines.text: You're standing in what it left. The black on these walls isn't paint, and the cracks aren't old age.
Outsiders make Withers now, from Hollowed skulls. Your folk. Would you ever?

replies.text: Good. Then you can stay. Say never again. Good.
Beat it? It doesn't fight, it burns! You don't beat fire. You just lose to it slower.
MAYBE? Out! No. Stay. But I'm watching your hands now.

lines: Ash-dark skin, Wither faces, and a name for every dead thing. They sat on the gold under the valleys like it was an egg.
The Withren remember every name they ever lost. We remember every bastion they burned. Fair trade.
A Withren never shouts. Never laughs. Never haggles. How do you trust somebody like that? You don't.
They light everything with soul fire. Blue, cold, nasty stuff. We can't stand near it. They know that. They do it on purpose.

lines.text: Ever been to a Vigil? Did they bore you to death?

replies.text: Ha! They tried that on us for a whole war. When boring us didn't work, they made the Wither.
Don't go. Too quiet. A Piglin would go mad from all that quiet.
Kind. Kind is how they get you. Watch your back. Watch your gold.

lines: Lava-walkers. They ferried us to war for pay, and the Wither burned their Moorings for it. Bad bargain. Their own fault.
Gold melts on their skin. Imagine! Can't wear it, can't hold it. No wonder they shiver and grumble so much.
Their striders are fat and slow and full of good meat. We borrow one now and then. They call it raiding. We call it borrowing.
A Magmari never shows gold. So a Magmari is never a friend. Not my rule. Gold's rule.

lines.text: Did a Magmari ever ferry you anywhere?

replies.text: Ha! Did they haggle the whole way? They haggle the whole way. Count your fingers when you land.
Good. Walk on your own feet, wear your own gold, owe nobody. That's the Piglin way.

lines: Four arms, six eyes, and not one honest bone. Well. Plenty of bones. Ours. They took them after the war.
We climb the warped canopy for shroomlights. They drop nets on us. We cut the nets. They make more nets. It goes on and on.
They weave everything into one long cloth. History, they say. I bet we're in it, looking bad.

lines.text: Ever been caught in a Weft net?

replies.text: Lucky. They leave you hanging there and click at you. *click click* Like that. Awful.
Ha! Then you're one of us! We sit round the hearth and complain about it. Loudly.

lines: Pale, floaty, always crying. From below they look like ghast whelps, so the crossbows go up. Mostly they were whelps. Mostly.
They cry for everybody. Even for Piglins, I heard. Waste of tears. Nobody should cry for a Piglin. They should cheer.
The ghasts that shriek at our walls were Ghastkin once, they say. Then they should come and collect them.
A Ghastkin never wears gold. A pity. Gold would cheer them right up.
Hoglins: tusks, temper, and the best meat in the Nether. Like a Piglin, but less charming.
Wild ones we hunt. Penned ones we keep. Don't mix them up. The herder will bite you, not the hoglin.
Never bring warped fungus near the pens. Hoglins hate it. The herder hates you for it more.

lines.text: My hoglins? Beautiful. Every one. Even the one that ate my boot. Especially that one. Good taste.
Ever fought a hoglin?

replies.text: Ha! A hoglin-fighter! You're tougher than you look. You look soft.
Do it once. Then never again. That's how everyone learns.
JUST PIGS? Say that in the pens. Go on. I'll watch from up here.

lines: Gold blocks. Chests. Things older than the fire. And a Brute who'd eat you before you got halfway to any of it.

lines.text: Every Piglin in the Hold puts in. Every Piglin can count it. We count it a lot. It's the best game there is.

lines: The Hoard isn't for spending. It's for having. Having is the whole point. Your folk never understand having.
Take from the Hoard and every Piglin near comes for you, gold or no gold. That's the oldest law there is.

lines.text: The vaults below still hold the old Hoards. The fire couldn't eat the gold. It only melted it into new shapes.
Want to see the Hoard some time?

replies.text: Admire. From the gate. With your hands where the Brute can see them. Good answer.

replies.ask: I'd love a bit of it.
replies.text: THIEF TALK! I'll pretend I didn't hear that. Once.

lines.text: Brutes are the biggest and the meanest. They don't barter, they don't laugh. They carry axes and they stand there.
Every Hold keeps two Brutes. One at the Hoard, one on the horn. Both of them are glaring at you. Right now.
Brutes respect gold. Except in a bastion vault. Down there, gold is just what they take off your body.
Want a secret? Brutes are born small, like the rest of us. They just never stop being angry about it.
Me. Big. Axe. Done.
Brute doesn't talk much. Talk is for traders. Brute is for gates.
You. Strong?

replies.text: Hrm. Good.
Hrm. No. Brave, though. Brave is good.
Hrm. Then stay behind me.

lines: A Brute! No, a Bartermaster! No, a Brute who barters! Nobody would ever say no to me.
I'm going to have the biggest gold pile in the whole Hold. Bigger than the Hoard. Bigger than {neighbour}'s.
When my tusks come in I'm going to bite a hoglin back. The one that bit me. I know which one.

lines.text: Will you help me get rich? Please? Lots?

replies.text: YES! You're the best gold-wearer ever! I'm telling everyone!
Work? That's what grown-ups say. Boring grown-ups. Are you a boring grown-up?

lines: Hoglin riding! You climb on a little one and hold on. It bites. You win if you don't cry.
Snatch! You grab some gold and run. Grown-ups chase you. Best game in the Nether.
Horn! One of us is the horn and shouts, and everybody jumps on {neighbour}. They don't like this game.

lines.text: Secret: {neighbour} cried when their baby hoglin ran off. Big crying. Don't tell. I didn't tell you.

lines: Not scared of anything! Except the blue fire. And the Rotted. And the Brute on the horn when he sneezes.
Grown-ups say if you go through a portal you come back Rotted. I'm never going. Unless there's gold. Then maybe.
Ghasts! They cry so loud. I hide under the bench. Not scared. Just hiding bravely.

lines.text: Secret: Brutes are scared of the blue fire too. I saw one jump. I didn't laugh. Out loud.

lines: I've got a nugget! Two nuggets! One's a pebble I rubbed on the other one. Don't tell.
I found a golden carrot. Well, I found it in {neighbour}'s hand. I ate it. It was hard on the teeth.
My treasure's buried under the hearth. Wait. Forget that. My treasure's somewhere else. Far away.

lines.text: Want to see my treasure? You have to say please.

replies.text: Hmm... NO! Ha! Maybe later. If you give me a nugget. Two nuggets.
THIEF! I'm telling! I'm telling the Brutes!

loved: GOLD! For me? Hold still, I need to look at it. *snort* Look at it! Everyone, look at it!
Ooh. Ohhh. Right now you're my favourite. Maybe forever. Let's say forever.
Now THAT is a handshake. You and I are going to get along.
I'll put it with my best things. Right next to my other best things. It'll be the best of them.

loved.text: For ME? Mine! Nobody touch it! *snort* It's the shiniest thing I've got!

liked: Good. Not gold, but good. I'll eat it, or wear it, or bite it. One of those.
Ha! You know what a Piglin likes. Not as well as gold, but close.
That'll do nicely. Hand it over. No, I'll take it. There.
Useful! I approve. I'd approve more if it shone.

liked.text: For me? Thank you! Is it gold next time?

neutral: What is it? Huh. Fine. I'll find a use. Or I'll throw it at {neighbour}.
That's not gold. Did you know that's not gold? Just checking.
Hm. Thanks. It goes on the pile of things that aren't gold. Big pile, that one.
A gift is a gift. Not a good one. But a gift.

neutral.text: Is it gold? It's not gold. Fine. I'll keep it anyway.

disliked: Get that away from me! What are you, a Withren?
Rot! Ash! Bad luck! Take it back. Take it far back.
Is this a joke? Ha. Ha. Not funny. Take it away before I get funny.
You hand a Piglin THIS? Walk carefully, gold-wearer.

disliked.text: Ew! No! That's horrible! I'm telling!

again: You already gave me something. I'm greedy, not stupid. Well. Greedy. Come back later.
Another one? Ha! Keep it for next time. I'll be just as greedy then.
No more! I'm still admiring the last one.
Slow down. Give me everything now and what will you bribe me with later?

again.text: You already gave me a thing! Grown-ups say one is polite. I say more is better. But fine.

empty: Your hand's empty. I can see it's empty. Why are you showing me an empty hand?
Nothing? You offer a Piglin nothing? Bold.
An empty hand is a sad thing. Fill it. With gold, ideally.
Ha! The old empty-hand trick. Very funny. Now give me something real.

empty.text: There's nothing in your hand! Is it invisible gold? Can I have the invisible gold?

levelup.text: You came back! Nobody comes back. Fine, you're a Shiny Stranger now. Here, five nuggets. Don't spend them. Admire them.
You came back! You're my Shiny Stranger! Here, a nugget. It's only a bit bitten.
Nugget-friend! I told {neighbour} all about you. Well, I said 'the shiny one'. Here, eat. Thin folk drop their gold.
Ingot-friend! Two ingots: one to keep, one to give back to me. That's friendship. And I know your face now. Gold or no gold, I won't swing at you.
Ingot-friend. Know your face now. No gold, fine. I won't swing. Vault's still mine.
Ingot-friend! Here, a whole ingot! And you don't have to be shiny for me now. I'll know it's you.
Hoard-friend. You may stand at the Hoard gate and nobody hits you first. Take my second-best sword. The best one is mine.
TUSK-KIN! Everyone hear it! Take this. Out of an old bastion vault, kept since the fire. Eat it or keep it. I'd keep it.
Tusk-kin. Take axe. Spare one. Good axe.
You're my Tusk-kin forever! Here, my best treasure. I found it. Mostly found it. Don't tell {neighbour}.

farewell: Keep your gold on out there. Somebody always wants it. Usually me.

farewell.text: Off you go, shiny. Don't take that gold off until you're far away. Very far.
Off you go. Put some gold on before you pass the others. They don't know you like I do.

farewell: Leaving already? Ha! Fine. I'll tell everyone you couldn't keep up.
Don't let your world rot you. Come back shining.

farewell.text: Bye! Bring gold next time! Lots!
Bye! *snort* Race you to the edge! I win!
Mind the broken bridges on your way out. The lava is patient.
Tell everyone {village} was the loudest Hold you ever saw. Because it was.
Go well, Tusk-kin. Anyone gives you trouble, tell me their name. I'll shout it at them.
Next time bring more ingots. I'm worth more ingots.

refuse.text: You hit me! Gold or no gold, I'm hitting back!
THIEF! Hoard-thief! Somebody blow the horn!
Your shiny helmet won't save you now!
Friend or not, you don't do that! Stand still so I can hit you!
Thief in the Bastion! To the vault, everyone! Don't let them out!
You're mean! I'm getting a Brute! A big one!
